## TL;DR

Task #1056 polishes the checks progress meter from #1054/#1047: full-width pill bars on board cards, half-width meters with inline labels in the drawer and pipeline status row, and shared track/fill styling so rounding and minimum sliver width stay consistent. Pipeline cards no longer gain an extra row when progress is countable; the drawer shows the remote host once.

## Work and rationale

Driver screenshots showed three layout problems with a common cause: native `<progress>` elements with fixed narrow widths and square caps, plus surface-specific markup that fought the desired grid. The board card capped the checks block at 320px, so the bar never reached the card’s inner edge and sat tight against the status line. The drawer pinned the meter to roughly 120px while centering the fraction label awkwardly to its right, and duplicated machine identity in both the scope line and the footer (`on remote host · remote host`). The pipeline placed `ChecksProgressDisplay` below row 3, adding a fifth visual band and breaking the card’s fixed rhythm.

The fix keeps `ChecksProgressDisplay.vue` as the single component for card, drawer, and pipeline, but replaces bare `<progress>` painting with a shared DOM meter: `.check-progress-meter__track` and `.check-progress-meter__fill` with pill radii, a visually hidden native `<progress>` for semantics, and `fillPercent` clamped to at least 2% so tiny fractions still show a visible rounded sliver. Width modifiers `.checks-progress-meter--full` and `.checks-progress-meter--half` live in global `style.css` so teleported card DOM and drawer/pipeline surfaces share the same caps.

For the card variant, `.checks-progress-display--card` stretches column-wide at `width: 100%` with a 7px gap between meter and `task-card-check-status-line`, plus the existing 8px top margin on `.task-card-check-progress`. The drawer bar row is a flex line: half-width meter on the left, left-aligned ellipsis detail on the right. `drawerChecksDisplay` stops appending the machine to `scopeWhereLine` when it is not a full check — the footer still renders `on ${machine}` once. Pipeline `ChecksProgressDisplay` moves into `pl-row-3` when `checkProgressPercent` is non-null, passing `stepLabel` as `pipelineStatusText` beside the meter; chip states and dot+step fallback stay on the same row, preserving four rows total.

## Approaches tried

An earlier #1054 layout widened native `progress` and used pipeline-only classes. That could not get pill caps on the fill in every engine without custom painting, and pipeline still used a dedicated row. Consolidating on track/fill divs plus hidden `<progress>` matches patterns elsewhere in the app and keeps theme tokens on `--accent-foreground` for the fill.

Pipeline integration briefly kept the bar under row 3 with smaller height only; that still violated the “same card height” acceptance criterion. Inlining into row 3 with `pl-check-progress { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; }` and ellipsis on `.checks-progress-pipeline-status` keeps elapsed time on the right via the existing spacer.

## Challenges and blockers

Scoped styles from #1047 had left card meters unstyled when rules lived only in drawer scoped CSS; this task relies on global `.check-progress-meter*` rules so TaskCard teleports stay covered. A prior agent turn ended on a network error before handoff; implementation was already on the branch in a WIP checkpoint. One handoff attempt reported UI verification passed for all three shots, then failed at a later verify step with a browser-capture timeout — environmental, not a missing selector.

## Key learnings

When one Vue component serves multiple surfaces, put visual variants in global CSS modifier classes rather than per-surface pixel widths on native form controls — especially for progress, where `accent-color` alone does not round the fill. For pipeline cards with a fixed row count, treat countable check progress as a substitute for the status dot+label row, not an add-on row. Machine/host copy belongs in a single line in the drawer footer; scope lines should name the check mode only so remote validation strings are not echoed twice.
